title: Cap. 7 Scholastici close: Suarez and Vasquez before Reformed Theologi nostri
pass_a_gloss: 9. I come to the Jesuits, who however they defend universal grace and universal redemption, yet do not dare to deny this special and efficacious ordination and intention of the saving passion as to the elect alone. For the rest let two of the foremost speak, Suarez and Vasquez. Suarez, on Aquinas part 3, question 19, Disputation, page 635, section 41. Just as Christ prayed in diverse manners for human beings, so he merited in diverse manners, for some sufficiently, for others efficaciously. Wherefore, although he is the universal Redeemer of all, and a sufficient cause of salvation, yet in a special manner he is the efficacious cause of the salvation of those whom he makes obedient to himself. For it is incredible that Christ offered his merits no otherwise for those whom he knew to be elect by the Father than for others, when he saw it to be the Father's will that they be saved infallibly, and not others. Suarez grants us that Christ's death and merits are efficacious unto the elect's salvation from the special manner of offering and the will of the offerer, not from a casual or contingent act of the human will apprehending it. 10. Vasquez clearly acknowledges this special intention of Christ as to the elect in the application of his merits, on Aquinas 1, question 23, disputation 49, chapter 3, page 687. I do not doubt that Christ by a peculiar prayer and will applied his merits to those who were predestined and elect. The same, on Aquinas 3, question 19, disputation 77, chapter 5, page 384, brings in Andreas Vega asserting that Christ's merits do not profit all efficaciously, because for those (to whom they do not profit) Christ did not pray efficaciously, nor offer his passion. We have therefore not only the ancient Fathers, but even the newer Papists themselves confessing what we are trying to demonstrate, namely that Christ's death is so constituted by God a universal cause of salvation applicable to all, that meanwhile, through a certain special intention of the offerer and accepter, it is constituted a particular cause of salvation to be applied infallibly and singularly to all and only the elect. See also Malderus, Antisynod, page 138.
pass_b_english: 9. Next the Jesuits. However they defend universal grace and universal redemption, they dare not deny this special, effectual ordination and intention of the saving passion toward the elect alone. Let two chiefs speak: Suarez and Vasquez. Suarez on Aquinas III q.19 (Disp. p. 635 §41): as Christ prayed diversely for humans, so he merited diversely — for some sufficiently, for others effectually. So though he is everyone's universal Redeemer and a sufficient cause of salvation, in a special way he is the effectual cause of salvation for those he makes obedient. It is incredible he offered his merits no differently for those he knew the Father had elect than for others, when he saw the Father's will was that they be saved without fail, and not others. Suarez thus grants that Christ's death and merits save the elect from the special mode of offering and the offerer's will — not from a chance act of human will laying hold of them. 10. Vasquez clearly owns this special intention toward the elect in applying his merits (on Aquinas I q.23, disp. 49, c.3, p. 687): I do not doubt Christ by peculiar prayer and will applied his merits to those predestined and elect. The same on Aquinas III q.19, disp. 77, c.5, p. 384, cites Andreas Vega: Christ's merits do not profit all effectually, because for those they do not profit he did not pray effectually or offer his passion. So not only the old Fathers but even newer Romanists confess what we aim to prove: God constituted Christ's death a universal saving cause applicable to all, yet by a special intention of offerer and accepter it is also a particular saving cause to be applied without fail, and singularly, to all and only the elect. See also Malderus, Antisynod, p. 138.
source_text: 9. Venio ad Jesuitas, qui utcunque universalem gratiam, & universalem redemtionem defendant, tamen hanc specialem & efficacem salutiferae passionis ordinationem & intentionem quoad solos electos non audent inficiari. Pro reliquis loquantur duo ex antesignanis, Suarez, & Vasquez. Suarez, in 3. Aquin. qu. 19. Disp. pag. 635. §. 41. Sicut Christus diversimode pro hominibus oravit, ita diversimode meruit, aliis sufficienter, aliis efficaciter. Propter quod, licet omnium sit universalis Redemtor, & sufficiens causa salutis, speciali tamen modo est causa efficax salutis eorum, quos sibi facit obedientes. Incredibile enim est, non aliter obtulisse Christum sua merita pro illis, quos sciebat esse electos a Patre, quam pro aliis, cum videret esse Patris voluntatem ut illi infallibiliter salvarentur, & non alii. Largitur nobis Suarez, Christi mortem ac merita esse efficacia ad salutem electorum ex speciali modo oblationis & voluntate offerentis, non ex casuali seu contingente actu humanae voluntatis eam apprehendentis. 10. Vasquez hanc specialem Christi intentionem quoad electos in applicatione meritorum suorum clare agnoscit, in 1. Aquinat. qu. 23. disp. 49. cap. 3. pag. 687. Ego non dubito Christum peculiari oratione & voluntate merita sua illis applicasse, qui praedestinati & electi fuerunt. Idem, in 3. Aquinat. qu. 19. disp. 77. cap. 5. pag. 384. inducit Andream Vegam asserentem, merita Christi non omnibus efficaciter prodesse, quia pro illis (quibus non prosunt) efficaciter Christus non oravit, nec obtulit suam passionem. Habemus igitur non solum antiquos Patres, sed ipsos etiam Papistas neotericos fatentes, quod nos demonstrare conamur, nimirum, Christi mortem sic a Deo constitutam universalem causam salutis omnibus applicabilem, ut interim, per specialem quandam intentionem offerentis & acceptantis, constituatur particularis causa salutis omnibus & solis electis infallibiliter & singulariter applicanda. Vide etiam Malderi Antisynod. pag. 138.
